page: Microsoft Azure M96bs_v3 is a memory-optimized server belonging to the MBSMediumMemoryv3 family. It features 96 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 48 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8473C processor running at 4.0 GHz. The architecture is x86_64, supported by a 105 MB L3 cache and advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). It is equipped with 768.0 GB of system memory, providing a ratio of 8.0 GB of RAM per core. The server does not include local storage or GPUs, relying instead on external block storage and Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization.

Benchmark results indicate top-tier memory performance, with uncached read-only memory bandwidth reaching 428.2 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 184.37 GB/sec. Multi-core processing capabilities are strong, as demonstrated by a Passmark CPU score of 97408.44 and a stress-ng multi-core performance value of 91332.66. The system also excels in database operations and static web serving, achieving top-tier ratings in both categories. For AI workloads, the server delivers strong performance in LLM inference prompt processing, handling up to 255.25 tokens/sec for medium-sized models.

The primary tradeoff of the M96bs_v3 is the complete absence of local storage and dedicated GPU hardware, which limits its suitability for local-disk-dependent tasks or heavy graphics processing. However, its high memory density and strong multi-core compute capabilities make it highly cost-efficient for memory-intensive enterprise workloads. It is best suited for large-scale relational databases, in-memory data stores, high-throughput static web serving, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
